note: Language pack for Classical Latin. Every URL and extraction rule is data — edit here, no recompile. No transcription scheme is declared, because a Latin headword is read from its own letters. Headwords are typed with their macrons, as a learner writes them, while every source keys its entries on the bare spelling; 'spelling' declares ordered regex rewrite pairs that recast the headword into the spelling the sources key on before it fills {word} in any URL or match pattern, and every source list of the pack shares them. Here they drop the macron and the breve from each vowel, since the stored headword keeps them. The varieties are the two readings Wiktionary prints for every Latin entry, the reconstructed Classical one and the modern Italianate Ecclesiastical one, labelled by name since no flag stands for a period. No respelling is declared, because the Classical reading is already written in plain IPA. No morphology sources are listed, because no vocabulary.json declares the paradigms yet.

pronunciation.name: Wiktionary
pronunciation.note: The Latin pronunciation list of an entry carries one line per reading, each opened by an accent label linking to the Classical Latin article or ending in Ecclesiastical, and closed by the IPA span. Each reading anchors on its label and takes the first IPA span after it, so the other languages sharing the spelling, which carry no such labels, stay out. A page listing several Latin forms, such as rosa and rosā, prints the headword's own list first, so the first match is the headword's. The span strategy is used because the transcription may nest a note span. The article page is asked before the mobile page, because the REST host rejects bursts with 429.

audio.name: Wikimedia Commons
audio.note: Latin recordings on Commons are La-cls- files in the Classical reading, La-ecc- files in the Ecclesiastical reading, and Lingua Libre LL-Q397 (lat)- files in whichever reading the speaker chose, and Wiktionary never embeds them, so the file store is searched directly. The search only joins terms with and, so each family is its own attempt, and the source keeps asking until both varieties are filled. Each search asks for files whose title carries the headword and the family tag, and the API answers with the transcoded renditions of each file found. Search matches by word, so each pattern takes only a file whose title ends in exactly {word}, allowing the part-of-speech suffix some La-cls- files carry, such as corium-noun. Only the mp3 rendition is taken, because the original is Ogg Vorbis or WAV. utf8=1 keeps the title readable so the headword can be matched, and formatversion=2 keeps the addresses unescaped. The Lingua Libre recording carries no reading, so it is shown once under every variety.

frequency.name: Logeion
frequency.note: Logeion's info API, the same call its sidebar makes, answers with the headword's rank in the Latin corpus of the PhiloLogic texts as a sentence, the 304th most frequent word, or unranked when it appears fewer than 50 times. The pattern keeps the figure or the word unranked, so the bands can read either. A spelling Logeion does not know is unranked too, so a typo is shown as rare rather than as nothing.
